gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, at maker-store prices on 2026-11-13, self-heating RV capacity is cheapest in the large LiTime LiHeat sizes: the 12V 320Ah Mini is $773.99 for 4,096 Wh ($189/kWh) and the 460Ah Mini is $1,034.99 for 5,888 Wh ($176/kWh). That is about half the $367/kWh of ChatGPT's 'premium cold-weather' Renogy 200Ah Pro, which is now in stock at $939.99, not the $1,164.99 pre-order ChatGPT showed. The 320Ah heated pack also costs only about 5% more per kWh than ChatGPT's unheated 'best overall value' LiTime 230Ah Bluetooth at $530.99 ($180/kWh), which stops charging below 32°F.
standout_why: I compared three pages. The cited BatteryTrail spec database (2026-11-06) gives prices only per 100Ah, and only for 100Ah-class units plus the Battle Born GC3. It has no 200Ah+ heated batteries and no $/kWh. The cited BoondockMaps page (updated 2026-07-17) and VanPowerCalc page (2026-03-10) give price ranges for 100–105Ah units, plus one unheated LiTime 200Ah at $349–399. Neither has a dated price for any heated battery above 105Ah or any per-kWh comparison. None of them lists the Renogy 200Ah Pro, the LiTime LiHeat 320Ah or 460Ah, or the LiTime 230Ah. ChatGPT's own cards had two prices that are now stale: the LiTime 230Ah Bluetooth at $589.99 (now $530.99) and the $1,164.99 pre-order Renogy (now $939.99).
decides: This changes the cold-weather pick and confirms the value pick. RV owners who camp in freezing weather and have room for a 14.5 × 7.4 × 10 in pack should take the LiTime LiHeat 320Ah Mini ($773.99). It has heating, 4,096 Wh and a 200 A BMS. Per kWh it costs about half as much as the Renogy 200Ah Pro ($939.99 for 2,560 Wh), and buys 1.6× the energy for $166 less. Per kWh it is also 22–52% cheaper than the Epoch 105Ah Essential ($549 for 1,340 Wh) and the heated Battle Born BB10012H ($999 for 100Ah). Mild-weather RVers should still take the LiTime 230Ah, at $530.99 with Bluetooth or $484.49 for the Plus without it. Battle Born wins only on its 10-year US-assembled warranty: its base 100Ah costs $799, versus $484.49 for 230Ah from LiTime. Among our own products, two Redodo 12V 100Ah Self-Heating units cost $503.98 for 2,560 Wh ($197/kWh), the cheapest heated option at the 200Ah level among those I priced. Each unit has a 100 A BMS.
